title: Inside Modern Server Hardware
summary: Move from naming server parts to relating hardware choices to a workload.
objectives: Identify major server hardware components and their roles.
Explain why a hardware choice depends on the work a system must perform.

vocab.def: A network interface that connects a computer to a network.
The size and shape standard of a device or component.
The computing work a system is asked to perform.

sections.heading: A server is a system of parts
sections.body: A motherboard connects components. A CPU processes general instructions. Memory supports active work. Storage keeps information. A NIC provides a network connection, and fans help move heat.

sections.heading: Hardware follows the workload
sections.body: A file service, a video service, and an AI workload may need different balances of processing, memory, storage, network capacity, and power. There is no single best server for every task.

sections.heading: Safe hardware exploration
sections.body: Use a labeled diagram or an approved unpowered training model. Do not open energized equipment, remove power supplies, or handle production hardware. Hands-on equipment work requires supervised instruction.

practice.prompt: Choose the most important hardware consideration for a file service, a large calculation, and a network-heavy service. Explain each choice.

quiz.question: What does a NIC provide?
options: A network connection for a computer
quiz.answer: A network connection for a computer

lab.objective: Label an approved server diagram and connect parts to a workload.
